elements.title: Choisir le jour
elements.note: Propose a day with « On se voit… ? », or leave it open with « Quand tu veux » (« Quand vous voulez » with vous).

items.cue: Théo, a friend, texts you. He says tu to you. You're free on Saturday.

turns.speaker: server
turns.name: Théo
turns.text: Salut ! On se voit quand ?

drills.prompt: What does Théo want to know?
Suggest Saturday, if that works for him.
drills.model: On se voit samedi, si tu veux !

items.cue: Inès, a colleague, texts you. She says tu to you. You have no plans that evening.

turns.speaker: server
turns.name: Inès
turns.text: On se voit vendredi soir ?

turns.speaker: learner
turns.text: Oui, vendredi, je suis ___ !

why: You are one person, so no -s.
« Calme » means calm, not free.

items.cue: Théo, a friend, texts you. He says tu to you. You're free on Friday evening too.

turns.speaker: server
turns.name: Théo

drills.prompt: Say you're free too, then suggest Friday evening.
drills.model: Moi aussi ! On se voit vendredi soir ?

items.cue: Léa, your flatmate, says tu to you. You'd like to go on Saturday evening.

turns.speaker: server
turns.name: Léa
turns.text: On va au cinéma ? Quand tu veux !

turns.speaker: learner
turns.text: Samedi soir, ça te ___ ?

why: « Ça » takes the il form: « ça te dit ».
« Dire » is the infinitive; « ça » needs a verb form.

drills.prompt: What does Léa say about the day?

items.cue: Théo writes to the group chat. He says tu to you. You're only free on Friday.

turns.speaker: server
turns.name: Théo

Sunday is « dimanche ».

items.cue: Mme Dumas, your landlady, wants to come by the flat. She says vous to you. Any day suits you.

turns.name: Mme Dumas

why: Too casual: « top » is for friends.
